variant_answers.text: The name states the behaviour: duplicates are removed so that each value is kept once, as its first occurrence (so [1, 2, 3, 2, 4] gives [1, 2, 3, 4]); this contradicts the docstring sentence of R-RM-1 and the example of R-EX-1.
The return annotation only describes the type of the value when the function returns; raising an exception on some inputs is not excluded.

variant_answers.phrase: remove all elements that occur more than once
variant_answers.text: Only the repeated (extra) occurrences are removed, so each value that occurs more than once is kept exactly once (the reading suggested by the function name remove_duplicates in R-SIG-1, which contradicts the example of R-EX-1).

variant_answers.phrase: From a list of integers, remove
variant_answers.text: The elements are deleted from the given list in place, and that list is returned.

variant_answers.phrase: Keep order of elements left the same as in the input
variant_answers.text: The remaining elements keep their original positions (indices) in the list.
Under the deduplicating reading of R-RM-1 and R-SIG-1, a kept value is ordered by the position of its first occurrence in numbers.
The example contradicts the function name remove_duplicates of R-SIG-1, under which the call would return [1, 2, 3, 4].
